lines: I could draw the route back with my eyes closed. I would rather not walk it again tonight.
For a moment, every direction looked wrong. Then home looked possible again.
I know the way home on paper. Knowing it while <dark_gray><wavy>scared</wavy></dark_gray> is different.
Every landmark looked strange in the dark. Then the village lights found me.
I would mark that route in red if I ever had to draw it.
The map says the road is short. My feet disagree.
I came back with no new map, only a better respect for old paths.
For once, I was glad the village was exactly where I left it.
I remember the moment I realized running was no longer possible.
My hands shook afterward more than they did during the fight.
I followed the creek because it was the only landmark the smoke could not hide.
The compass shook in my hand hard enough to make north look uncertain.
I abandoned the straight road when I saw movement along the ridge.
One fallen marker told me I was closer to home than fear claimed.
I used the map case as a shield for one very long second.
The fight pushed me off every route I had planned.
I kept the village bell on my left until the trees opened.
A shortcut through the ditch saved time and nearly cost me an ankle.
I will add that ruined wall as cover on every working map from now on.
Getting home taught me which landmarks remain useful while running.
